findings.scenario: Legal config maxAttempts=2: attempt 0 is `retryable-failure`, control plane claims index 1, attempt 1 is `completed` with a schema-valid unapplied typed proposal, segment still `active`, no live handle. HITL entry fails because attempt 0 remains `retryable-failure`. The mutex then forbids `active -> completed|failed|budget-exhausted`, so the only legal close is operational cancel. The typed proposal never gets `active -> interrupted`, so the four hashes are never written and unique live acceptance cannot close completed.
findings.remediation: When claiming attempt index 1, settle attempt 0 out of `retryable-failure` into a terminal attempt record, and evaluate HITL only against the current attempt plus live `claimed`/`in-flight`/`ambiguous` handles. A completed current attempt with a schema-valid unapplied proposal must still take `active -> interrupted` after a successful same-route retry.

findings.line: `interrupted -> interrupted` ... invalid; mismatch cancels rather than rebinds
findings.scenario: Segment is `interrupted` with write-once hashes H1/P1/E1. A duplicate worker delivery or any CAS that repeats `active -> interrupted` / stays in `interrupted` / supplies different hashes is both “invalid” (must reject/attach, no transition) and “mismatch cancels”. If mismatch-cancel wins, one duplicate or rewrite attempt CASes `interrupted -> cancelled`, emits a terminal receipt, and drops HITL without a unique accept/reject decision. That races the human decision and violates otherwise-cancellation only after the live accept/reject path.
findings.remediation: Split the rules: `interrupted -> interrupted` and duplicate/self CASes reject or attach with zero mutation. The four hashes stay immutable for the life of the segment record, including terminal states. Only a listed `interrupted -> cancelled` trigger (reject/expiry/revocation/stale expected state) or a failed `accept-proposal` live-gate compare may cancel; hash mismatch on accept cancels, hash mismatch on duplicate interrupt delivery does not.

audit.proof_assessment: HEAD equals BASE; only the S2 planning contract changed. The attached Grok PROPOSAL-HITL FINDINGS describe an older hole set (`active -> completed` still beside HITL; hashes not write-once). Current bytes close those two items with the typed-proposal mutex, write-once four-hash rule, and forbidden `interrupted -> interrupted`. They are evidence of prior review, not authority over these bytes. Remaining criterion pressure is the HITL entry predicate after retry and the cancel-vs-reject conflict on hash mismatch/duplicate CAS. S3 decision-slot text is adjacent evidence, not this allowlist.
residual_risks: `active -> interrupted` is specified as a multi-record CAS (segment, settled attempt, interrupt, proposal, expected state, held reservation) with no single closed transaction record; in-memory fixtures cannot prove durable atomicity.
RouteSegmentStateV1 has no decisionHash; unique `accept-proposal` uniqueness is deferred to the S3 slot CAS.
`interrupted -> completed` requires the reservation still held and never reconciles it, so accept can leak budget.
Kill-switch on or reservation loss during `interrupted` is an accept live-gate failure but is not named as a mandatory `interrupted -> cancelled` trigger.
Leftover “Resume or cancellation” wording can be misread as `interrupted -> active` even though that transition is unlisted.
